item.title: Chance The Rapper’s SocialWorks Sets 11-Site Chicago Winter Drive
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Chance the Rapper's SocialWorks announced a winter supply drive with 11 Chicago collection sites and a January 10 deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Chance the Rapper‘s SocialWorks is asking Chicago residents to help stock 11 collection sites with winter supplies for people experiencing homelessness.

The nonprofit’s ninth annual Warmest Winter clothing drive will run from November 2, 2026, through January 10, 2027. Its wish list includes coats, jackets, scarves, gloves, hats, blankets and socks, either new or gently used.

Toys can also be new or gently used. Hygiene products must be new, including soap, deodorant, toothpaste and toothbrushes. Diapers, baby clothes and other baby essentials are welcome. Food and canned goods are not accepted.

“For nine years, Warmest Winter has brought Chicagoans together around a simple belief: everyone deserves warmth, dignity, and care,” SocialWorks said in its announcement.

The effort has drawn support from Chicago students and adult donors. During the previous winter season, Owen Elementary’s Class of 2026 collected eight bags for SocialWorks’ closet, Chicago Public Schools said in a February update.

The Ashburn school’s donations included shoes, cold-weather clothing, hygiene supplies and baby items. It was Owen’s third year taking part in the drive.

Warmest Winter also reaches beyond the annual collection period. SocialWorks describes it as a year-round effort for people facing homelessness and extreme hardship, with volunteer work and outings alongside its clothing drive and holiday event.

Its SocialThreads clothing pantry, run in collaboration with Chicago’s Department of Family and Support Services, offers free clothes, toys and hygiene supplies. People can choose items that fit their own needs and style.

Chance’s winter fundraising goes back more than a decade. In January 2016, AllHipHop covered his Warmest Winter campaign, which raised $100,000 to help provide coats for Chicago residents experiencing homelessness.

This May, the rapper was among those honored at TIME’s philanthropy impact dinner in New York City. He spoke there about the responsibility that comes with that recognition, calling for continued care for children.

“We’re continuing to look out for the children, that we are building a world that’s safe for them,” Chance said at the May 21 event.

For this season’s donations, SocialWorks’ announcement includes a collection-site map. Donors should check building access and holiday hours before heading out.

item.title: Ice-T Dismisses Parenting Critics With Two Blunt Words
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ice-T and Coco Austin have faced years of scrutiny over raising Chanel, whose school milestones have also played out online.
item.content:encoded:
Ice-T told E! News “F–k ’em” when asked about parenting critics at Heidi Klum’s Halloween party.

The rapper and actor has spent years defending how he and Coco Austin raise Chanel while sharing parts of their family life online. He compared their household to another famous family’s and pushed back against treating all parents the same.

“We’re like the Osbournes. We have a different dynamic in our house. But it’s not harmful. That’s the main thing. It’s us,” he said in a previous interview.

Chanel is his youngest child and his only child with Austin, following his older daughter, LeTesha and son, Tracy Jr., from previous relationships.

The couple’s choices drew criticism in 2022 when Austin shared footage of Chanel bathing in a kitchen sink before heading to a fashion show.

The child was six at the time, and Austin explained that using the sink helped her get ready faster.

She defended the decision in an interview with Page Six, telling the outlet, “Everything I do, people have got to say something about it.”

That year also brought complaints about Austin using a stroller for Chanel, adding another dispute over a routine family outing to the public discussion.

An earlier argument centered on Austin breastfeeding Chanel at five, which she described as a source of comfort and closeness for her daughter.

“Chanel still likes my boobs. It’s a big bonding moment for a mother and your child,” Austin told Us Weekly in 2021.

Austin said Chanel also ate meals and sometimes wanted to nurse, explaining that she would let her daughter decide when to stop.

The public family updates have also included school milestones, with Austin sharing Chanel’s fourth-grade graduation picture on Instagram in June and reflecting on time passing.

She joked about gathering mothers for a group where they could share that feeling over coffee or tea, even suggesting tequila as another option.

“To all the moms who blinked and suddenly their little baby is graduating another grade-I’m right there with you,” Austin wrote.

Chanel, who was born November 28, 2015, will celebrate her 11th birthday later this month.

item.title: Ja Rule Rethinks Slowing Down After Alicia Keys’ Clive Davis Tribute
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ja Rule weighed more time with his family before a tribute to Clive Davis gave him a fresh view of his future in music.
item.content:encoded:
Ja Rule reconsidered slowing down his career after Alicia Keys’ tribute to Clive Davis made him see another path for his next chapter.

In a Jerusalem Post interview, the Hip-Hop veteran explained how hearing about Davis’ late-career comeback changed his plans for the years ahead.

“I learned a lot there. I left feeling truly inspired,” he said of Davis’ funeral and the tributes he heard there.

At 50, Ja Rule had been weighing time with his children and granddaughter Bella against the pace that kept him working through their childhoods.

Keys’ account of Davis starting again at 67 gave him a different way to think about age and the years ahead.

“And at that moment, I realized I wasn’t done yet,” he said, recalling how her tribute changed his thoughts that day.

Davis’ Manhattan funeral took place June 29, with Ja Rule among the artists gathered at Central Synagogue to honor the executive.

Alicia Keys, Dionne Warwick, Barry Manilow and Stevie Wonder also attended, while Bruce Springsteen spoke and Jennifer Hudson sang at the private service.

The ceremony was streamed for the public, bringing together performers whose careers crossed different styles but shared a link to Davis’ work.

Ja Rule’s concerns about time with family follow an earlier public adjustment to his new role as a grandfather and how he announced it.

He had revealed the pregnancy to Sherri before acknowledging that he might have spoken before his family intended.

“Big mouth, big papa. Spilled all the beans,” he joked.

Ja Rule also connected his desire to be present for his family to growing up without his father, whose absence shaped his approach.

Asked what he wanted to achieve in that role, he answered, “Being the best grandfather that I could be.”

His trip also put him back before a live audience, with an October 29 set at Hangar 11 drawing on songs including “Mesmerize” and “New York.”

item.title: Nelly Turns To Ashanti For Cash After Losing At Spades To Michael Jordan
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nelly recalled asking Ashanti for cash after he and his brother lost a spades game against Michael Jordan and Charles Oakley.
item.content:encoded:
Nelly had to ask Ashanti for money after a spades game against Michael Jordan left him short on cash, with his wife there to see him lose.

The rapper recalled the night on “7PM in Brooklyn with Carmelo Anthony,” where he joined Anthony, Monica and Kaz. The episode was released October 30 in the United States.

He and his younger brother had teamed up against Jordan and Charles Oakley. Nelly remembered winning early, then talking trash. Ashanti’s presence helped encourage the boasting, he explained, before the game turned in the other team’s favor.

“He did it in front of my woman,” Nelly said before asking Ashanti, “lost a lot of money that night. Babe, what you got in that pocket?” he recalled.

Oakley reminded him that he had warned him about talking too much. Still, Nelly described the experience warmly, recalling how much he enjoyed being welcomed into that circle.

The rapper and Jordan have both held stakes in the Charlotte Bobcats. AllHipHop reported in July 2004 that Nelly had become a part-owner alongside Bob Johnson. Jordan later joined the ownership group, then moved to take control of the team.

The NBA approved his purchase of a controlling interest on March 17, 2010. At the time of his investment, Nelly described owning part of the franchise as one of the biggest achievements of his career.

Fans will soon get more of Nelly and Ashanti’s life together through the second season of “Nelly & Ashanti: We Belong Together,” which premieres November 19 on Peacock. They are raising their toddler son Kareem, known as KK, while managing work that often takes them away from each other.

“We’re both on tour at different times, being in different places,” Nelly explained in the season’s trailer.

The series will also follow their decisions about showing their son on social media and the demands of a blended family.

Ashanti works on new recordings while Nelly deals with the physical strain of touring. Ashanti also moves between St. Louis and New York City as she balances motherhood, music and performances.

item.title: Kelly Rowland Sidesteps Destiny’s Child Reunion Question For Jay-Z’s Super Bowl
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kelly Rowland leaves Destiny's Child reunion plans to Jay-Z as he prepares for his first Super Bowl halftime performance.
item.content:encoded:
Kelly Rowland left the guest list to Jay-Z when asked whether Destiny’s Child would join his Super Bowl halftime show.

The singer faced the reunion question at the Airbnb.org Gala in Hollywood on October 28, with Jay’s SoFi Stadium booking already drawing attention.

“That’s none of my business,” Rowland told PEOPLE. “That’s his performance. That’s none of my business.”

Her answer offered no guest announcement, and neither Beyoncé nor Michelle Williams was named as part of a halftime reunion in those remarks.

Jay’s move to the halftime stage follows years of behind-the-scenes work through Roc Nation’s partnership with the NFL, which began in 2019.

AllHipHop previously covered his confirmed booking, which puts him in the lead role after his work on halftime sets headlined by other artists.

The same stadium hosted his October 23 and 24 anniversary concerts, where he marked three decades since Reasonable Doubt and 25 years since The Blueprint.

Those shows also brought his music family together, with guests across the two nights including John Legend, Scarface, Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and DJ Khaled.

Destiny’s Child already has a recent stage reunion to look back on, even without a new Super Bowl appearance on the books.

Beyoncé brought Rowland and Williams into her final Cowboy Carter concert at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on July 26, 2025.

Their set included “Lose My Breath” and “Bootylicious,” while the night also featured appearances from Jay-Z and Shaboozey during Beyoncé’s tour finale.

It was the trio’s first public stage performance together since Beyoncé’s 2018 Coachella set, making the Las Vegas show a return after seven years.

Williams later said on Watch What Happens Live that the Las Vegas reunion came together quickly, unlike their more planned Coachella performance.

“This one was, ‘Y’all let’s do this,’ and we did,” Williams said, recalling how the three agreed to share that stage again.

The singers have also stayed close away from work, sharing a meal this year to mark Williams’ Grammy nomination for Death Becomes Her.

“We just shared a meal, but we laughed until we were crying,” Rowland said on All Access with Linsey Davis.

Jay-Z’s halftime show is set for February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

item.title: GDP Reveals Why He Walked Away From Rap Without Saying Goodbye
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: GDP explained how label work drained his desire to rap and how time away helped him find his way back to making music.
item.content:encoded:
GDP walked away from rap without announcing a retirement. Now the New Jersey rapper has explained how running a label left him struggling to make music on his own.

In a new Bandcamp Daily interview, he described stepping away around 2017 as studio sessions in Brooklyn began to feel forced.

“After sending 20 emails half the day, you’re not inspired to write music,” he said.

He had been handling business for his Smoker’s Cough label. The question became simple: “Why am I doing this? I could just stop.”

The distance gave him room to work without a manager pushing him. It also took him toward documentary work for the global health nonprofit Emergency Project.

During the break, photography became part of how he made a living in New York City. Working as George Douglas Peterson, he made zines, photo books and music videos, with medical mission documentation among his projects.

He also continued playing drums in Ankle Monitor and making electrogrind as Orange Crystal. The hiatus from solo rap records still left room for other music.

Last year’s Endocrine with Fatboi Sharif had already opened a route back. Their collaboration began with GDP making beats for Sharif and grew into a friendship, live shows and a seven-song album.

Released July 11, 2025, through Fused Arrow Records, it featured both rappers’ writing and performances, with GDP producing as Orange Crystal. Sharif also appears on “Undone” on the new solo record.

GDP also spoke about Tame One’s mentorship, which began after they met when he was 18. That connection helped bring him into Young Zee’s studio circle.

Tame One died in 2022 at 52. The Artifacts MC made the group’s 1994 debut, Between a Rock and a Hard Place, with El Da Sensei and DJ Kaos.

GDP’s new solo album, Cross Off Matthew, came together in a walk-in closet studio.

Released October 23 through Run For Cover Records, the 12-song project was self-produced. Its songs deal with strained relationships, vices and the pressure that can come with making creative work.

The album closes with “Doom Loop,” which examines why he made music after relationships fell apart.

“I wanted to make something that felt nuanced, something that I could feel proud of,” GDP said in the label’s account of the record.

item.title: 2 Chainz Defends Celebrity Perks In Keith Lee Restaurant Debate
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 2 Chainz defended the perks of fame as Keith Lee stood by restaurant reviews based on how staff treated regular customers.
item.content:encoded:
2 Chainz defended the perks of fame in a disagreement with Keith Lee over restaurant reviews. Lee stood by judging the service a regular customer would get.

The two discussed Lee’s criticism of Esco Restaurant & Tapas on Kirk Franklin’s “Den of Kings.” For the rapper, better treatment came with the work he had put into his career. For the food reviewer, being recognized could change the very experience he was there to assess.

“I’m an entertainer, and obviously we get perks that other people don’t get. That’s just period, my boy,” 2 Chainz said.

He pointed to skipping airport lines as an example. He also questioned whether Lee’s diet as a former athlete shaped his restaurant judgments.

Lee defended sending relatives to place orders without revealing his identity. That allowed him to judge what paying customers could expect, rather than what staff would do for a famous guest.

The dispute involved a business 2 Chainz had built beyond music. He and partner Mychel “Snoop” Dillard had pursued Esco franchises outside Atlanta. Dillard described the concept in 2022: “We’re a restaurant during the day, lounge by night. That’s the culture we create.”

Lee’s stance had already shaped his 2023 Atlanta food trip, when he visited for ONE Music Fest. His complaints went beyond taste to whether people could order food or get a seat.

At Kandi Burruss’ Old Lady Gang, he said his family faced a 90-minute wait, only for staff to offer him a seat as soon as he entered. He left instead.

At The Real Milk and Honey, Lee said relatives were turned away for “deep cleaning” while other people picked up food. He said he again left after a server recognized him and offered service.

His trip also brought praise for Jamaican Jerk Biz, The Dining Experience and Juci Jerk.

item.title: Timbaland Demands Receipts After Ex-Manager Says He Blew His Fortune
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Timbaland's lawyer rejected Gary Marella's overspending account and alleged financial records and an approval email were altered.
item.content:encoded:
Timbaland‘s lawyer answered Gary Marella’s overspending claims Monday, November 2, accusing the producer’s former management team of failing to protect his money and pointing to allegedly altered records.

“Holding someone accountable for the responsibilities they were hired and paid to perform is not shifting blame,” attorney Tynia Coats told Rolling Stone.

Coats and Timbaland alleged that accounting records listed a consultant’s payment as $16,000 even though the consultant received $165,000. They also alleged that emails were changed to suggest Timbaland approved a $250,000 attorney payment when he had approved $100,000.

Coats and Timbaland also called for an accounting of how the producer supposedly spent the money Marella said his team brought in.

The response followed Timbaland’s October 30 lawsuit against Marella and business manager Bruce Seckendorf.

The producer sought $15 million, claiming the men mishandled his finances, collected excess commissions and left his mortgage unpaid. He alleged a 2025 foreclosure notice exposed the problems, which also included unpaid federal taxes and penalties.

Marella disputed the accusations in a statement. He said he began managing Timbaland in 2017, when the producer was already in debt, and helped generate roughly $75 million in business over about nine years.

He blamed Timbaland’s spending for his financial troubles and said the business manager handled the money and paid management commissions.

“The allegation that I paid myself without his knowledge is simply absurd. Managing his finances was not my role,” Marella said.

The suit reached across their business relationship, from commissions on Verzuz payments to the sale of Timbaland’s music catalog. It also accused Marella of mismanaging Beatclub, the marketplace the pair developed to connect music creators with established artists. Both managers were fired in 2025.

Marella had publicly backed the catalog deal when Hipgnosis announced it in October 2019. The acquisition covered a catalog comprising 108 albums and songs. Speaking as Timbaland’s manager at the time, Marella emphasized the buyer’s responsibility to creators.

“It’s important to all creators that their work is in the right hands,” Marella said.

Marella and Seckendorf did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the new allegations.

item.title: Flyysoulja’s New Condo & Car Celebration Ends With Drug Overdose
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Flyysoulja said a drug overdose sent him to a Miami trauma unit before his November 2 release from the hospital.
item.content:encoded:
Flyysoulja said a cocaine, benzodiazepine and Percocet overdose sent him to a Miami trauma unit on October 29. He was released November 2.

The Island Boys rapper, whose real name is Alex Venegas, told TMZ he had stopped using drugs before celebrating a new condo and car. He said he underwent an involuntary mental health evaluation under Florida’s Baker Act. He also described years of addiction.

Percocet combines the opioid oxycodone with acetaminophen, according to its drug label. In its safety warning on opioids and benzodiazepines, the FDA listed risks including “extreme sleepiness, respiratory depression, coma and death.”

The agency said both kinds of drugs affect the central nervous system, which controls most functions of the brain and body.

Flyysoulja had talked about a drug crisis at his home last year. In November 2025, he spoke to fans on Instagram Live after a three-day stay at a mental health center near Miami, as AllHipHop reported at the time.

He said he had taken multiple drugs before damaging his home. He also explained why viewers had seen the episode online: he had been broadcasting without realizing it.

“In the psychosis, I was trying to find something for my hair for hours, and destroyed the home while unknowingly being on Live,” he said.

He also challenged the basis for the police response. He claimed officers had entered the property without proper permission. He further alleged they had mistaken spilled nail polish for blood as they investigated the scene.

At the time, he said his drug use was the problem. He denied he had been suicidal. KaylaThayla, who shares a child with him, said she found out he had been taken in when she went to collect her pets from the house.

His brother and fellow Island Boy Kodiyakredd told fans he would bring Flyysoulja home once the exam was over.

Under the Baker Act, a person can be held for a mental health exam. Florida’s official Baker Act criteria require suspected mental illness, refusal or inability to decide about an exam because of that illness and serious risks of harm without care.

item.title: Cardi B Gives Johns Hopkins Students A ChatGPT Reality Check
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B urged Johns Hopkins students to pass their classes and leave ChatGPT out of the answers during her Hoptoberfest set.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B told Johns Hopkins University students to pass their classes without asking ChatGPT for the answers during her Hoptoberfest performance on Sunday, November 1.

“Y’all better pass y’all motherf–kin’ semester,” she told the crowd. “And don’t ask ChatGPT for the answer.”

The rapper took the stage after a last-minute headliner change. Daniel Caesar could no longer perform because of unspecified unforeseen circumstances.

Organizers HOP and LEED announced Cardi’s booking on October 31 and moved the concert from that night to Sunday at 8 p.m. at the Ralph S. O’Connor Center for Recreation & Well-Being.

The original show had sold out on October 21, with hundreds of students on the waitlist. Existing tickets remained valid after the switch. Caesar’s original booking had been announced on October 19, less than two weeks before students learned Cardi would take over.

“When they switched it to Cardi B, I was a little surprised and honestly thought it was fake,” student Bhavya Guru told The Johns Hopkins News-Letter.

As AllHipHop previously reported, the free concert continued a campus tradition that began in 2013. Past Hoptoberfest performers included Khalid in 2025, Rick Ross in 2023 and Desiigner in 2022.

Her campus remarks also followed an earlier complaint about AI content reaching her relatives. In a February 4 post on X, Cardi wrote, “Free my older family members from facebook Ai.”

At Johns Hopkins, one program has already laid out how AI can fit into schoolwork. The Engineering for Professionals program’s student guidance gives instructors several choices about what to allow in class.

The program describes courses that ban AI, courses that allow limited use with disclosure and courses that allow wider use with transparency. Students still have to answer for their own work. That includes checking AI output for errors and bias.

They may also have to say how they used the tools.

That guidance governs the Engineering for Professionals program, where acceptable AI use can vary by course and assignment. Students who do not know what an assignment allows are told to ask their instructor.

“Treat GenAI as a learning partner, not an authority,” the program advises.
